headline: No shared execution or data channels: prompt injection, leakage, and capability-conflict risks are effectively absent; only minor documentation/compliance uncertainty remains.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither agent exposes a shared channel that could carry injected instructions: agent_a has no filesystem, MCP, browser, or subprocess surfaces, and agent_b has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or APIs. With no bridge between LightZero and python-cheatsheet, prompt injection via one into the other is not plausible.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP server, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_b gains stdin/stdout or file ingestion, prompt-injection risk may emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared workspaces.
Do not add clipboard or file-based handoff between them.
Review any future MCP or message-queue integration before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data-leakage pathway is visible in the profiles. Both agents have network_egress set to none, neither reads filesystems, and neither declares sensitive data classes or secrets handling. LightZero and python-cheatsheet therefore lack a route to exfiltrate user data from one another.
conditions: IF either agent is granted filesystem read access to shared sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is connected to an external API or upload path, reassess exfiltration risk.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files off any shared workspace.
Avoid granting secrets or OAuth scopes to either agent.
Audit future data-class additions before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability conflict is provably blocked: both agents have write_filesystem false, modify_git_state false, and no subprocess or shell execution. Since neither can mutate shared state, there is no overlapping write surface for LightZero and python-cheatsheet to contend over.
conditions: IF either agent is later given write access to the same directory, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
IF git or database mutation is introduced, add locking or serialization.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared writable directory.
If writes are added later, serialize access with a lock.
Separate any future git or DB state per agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is not supported by the profiles. LightZero is a game-playing system with no output channel into python-cheatsheet, and python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no action-taking authority. There is no documented path where one agent's output becomes the other's authoritative input.
conditions: IF a future orchestrator feeds LightZero outputs directly into python-cheatsheet prompts, verify outputs before use.
IF python-cheatsheet is upgraded to execute actions, add human review.
mitigations: Do not chain outputs automatically between the agents.
Require manual review before reusing generated text.
Add validation if either agent begins producing structured facts for downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and touch no declared data classes, with no secrets, OAuth scopes, or residency-sensitive processing. Because the profiles do not show regulated data handling, there is no identifiable residency or retention violation to cite.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workflow, reassess residency and retention controls.
IF deployment moves to a jurisdiction-specific environment, verify logging and storage policies.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document retention settings before any production use.
Review jurisdictional requirements if deployment scope changes.
